===== ORIGINAL PROMPT (initial_prompt.md) =====
Build a visually stunning, fully offline iOS app called "Aura" — a
daily generative "vibe card." Native Apple stack only: SwiftUI +
SwiftData, Core Image / Metal (CIFilter compositions or a custom
Metal shader) for procedural generative art, Swift Charts for the
recap view, StoreKit 2 for local in-app purchases (no backend needed —
App Store handles receipts/entitlements locally). No accounts, no
network, no third-party SDKs — everything on-device, forever. Follow
the ios-app-factory-rules.

CONCEPT: once a day, the user answers 2-3 quick prompts (a mood
picker, one or two tap-to-select word/emoji chips, optionally the
on-device time of day). From that input plus a per-day deterministic
seed, generate a unique abstract generative-art "Aura" card — think
painterly gradient blooms, particle fields, or flow-field line art,
NOT a literal illustration — paired with a short generated caption
built from a curated local phrase bank (never a hallucinated/unsafe
LLM call — this is deterministic, on-device, and instant). The card
must look genuinely beautiful: this is the single most important
requirement in this build. If the generative output looks like
placeholder gradients or a design-101 exercise, the build has failed
its actual goal even if it compiles and passes gates.

CORE FEATURES (favor complete over broad):
1. Daily check-in flow: fast (under 10 seconds), delightful, satisfying
   micro-interactions (haptics, spring animations) on every tap. Once
   completed, locked until the next calendar day (device local time
   zone) — handle timezone travel and DST without allowing two cards
   the "same day" or skipping a day.
2. Generative card engine: a real, documented deterministic algorithm
   mapping (date seed + mood + chips) -> a reproducible but visually
   varied composition (palette, shape field, motion-blur/particle
   density). Same inputs on the same day always render the same card;
   different days must feel meaningfully different from each other,
   not like the same template recolored. This is the technical heart
   of the app — treat it with the same rigor as an algorithm module,
   not incidental UI.
3. Collection & streaks: a scrollable archive/grid of past cards
   (like a photo grid), a streak counter, and a "your Aura over time"
   trend view (mood distribution via Swift Charts).
4. Monthly/seasonal "Wrapped": after each calendar month, generate a
   shareable recap — a short animated sequence or a single composite
   poster of that month's dominant palette/mood story (Spotify-Wrapped
   style). This is a primary viral surface — must render as a
   beautiful, portrait (9:16) export.
5. Share export: every single card AND the monthly Wrapped must export
   as a high-resolution image (and ideally a short looping video/Live
   Photo-style clip of the generative animation) sized correctly for
   Instagram/TikTok Stories (1080x1920), via the native share sheet.
   A small, tasteful, dismissible-only-via-purchase watermark on free
   exports is the monetization hook (see below) — it must never be so
   intrusive it kills the shareability that drives virality.
6. Monetization (StoreKit 2, local only): one non-consumable "Aura+"
   unlock via native IAP removing the export watermark and unlocking
   extra palette themes + the ability to regenerate a card once per
   day if unsatisfied (free tier: no regeneration). Handle purchase,
   restore purchases, and the Simulator's inability to complete real
   StoreKit transactions honestly — use a local StoreKit configuration
   file for Simulator testing and say so explicitly, don't fake a
   purchase succeeding without going through StoreKit's real API.
7. Widget: home-screen widget showing today's card once generated, or
   an inviting "your Aura is waiting" state before check-in.
8. Notifications (local only, opt-in): a gentle daily reminder if the
   user hasn't checked in yet, respecting Focus/Do Not Disturb norms
   and permission denial gracefully.

PRIORITIES, in order: (a) the generative art must be genuinely
beautiful and varied — treat this as a design/craft problem, iterate
on the actual visual output, not just "does it render"; (b) the
deterministic seeding algorithm must be correct and tested (same
inputs -> same card, always); (c) the share-export pipeline must
produce real, correctly-sized, good-looking image/video files, not a
plain screenshot of the UI. Seed a "demo history" toggle with 30+ days
of varied past cards so the archive/Wrapped/trend screens are never
empty on first review. Provide a clear way to run it in the iOS
Simulator via Xcode, and honestly flag anything StoreKit-transaction-
related that cannot be fully verified without a real device/sandbox
account.

--- portfolio_selection (final decision) ---
Both Codex and Claude read this the same way from the start: this is one app, and the phase's real job here was to explicitly confirm that rather than manufacture a split. Codex framed it as a systems-coherence argument (check-in, seed engine, persistence, streaks, and export all share one state model — splitting them would break the daily ritual). Claude framed it as a user-experience argument (the person using this experiences one continuous object — open app, see today's Aura or check in, browse the grid, get Wrapped — and fragmenting that across projects serves internal tidiness, not the user). Both explicitly reject inventing extra apps (no "Aura Lite," no separate widget-app, no companion Watch app, no onboarding-shell app) just because the phase template implies portfolio thinking. No disagreement surfaced — this reads as genuine, immediate convergence on a call that was never really contested.

Claude used the rest of its turn productively: naming the actual failure mode to guard against (a technically-compliant build that reads as "nice SwiftUI gradient exercise" rather than something worth having) and proposing three concrete, checkable success bars for the eventual build/verify phases — first card in under 10 seconds of interaction with no forced tutorial, archive/trend views feeling alive by day 3 of seeded history (not empty-state-as-feature), and a share export that would actually get posted rather than screaming "placeholder." These aren't new decisions in tension with anything — they're operationalizations of what prompt_contract and product_research already locked in (beauty as the hard gate, demo history as non-empty-by-design), stated here because this is the last checkpoint before implementation starts.

  rejected: Using default SwiftUI List/Picker/NavigationStack chrome for speed of implementation
  constraints: Build phase must implement custom grid, custom picker shapes, and custom top bar rather than stock components
- [DEC-design_discussion-005] Today screen has six distinct states: cold-launch skeleton, not-yet-checked-in (dim unlit aura silhouette), check-in steps (mood then chip, time-of-day resolved silently), bloom reveal, settled revealed state (with regeneration visibly gated, not hidden, for free users), and a store-load-failure error state visually and textually distinct from the genuine new-user empty state.
  rationale: Conflating a store-load failure with a genuine empty state would silently read as data loss, the exact failure mode already warned against upstream; showing free users a visibly-gated (not hidden) regenerate affordance surfaces the paid feature as a real upsell rather than an invisible one.
  rejected: Treating store-load failure and new-user-empty as the same UI state; Hiding the regenerate affordance entirely for free-tier users
  constraints: Widget tap must deep-link to whichever of these six states is currently true, not just foreground the app to a default screen
- [DEC-design_discussion-006] Archive grid cells carry the demo-history badge directly on the cell itself, in addition to a dismissible top banner while demo mode is active; a genuine empty state is a designed icon+line+CTA, never bare 'no cards yet' text.
  rationale: Banners get scrolled past; the grid must remain self-explanatory about demo-vs-real status even after a user forgets the banner exists, per the already-locked demo-labeling requirement.
  rejected: Relying solely on a top banner to indicate demo mode is active
  constraints: Applies per-cell in the archive grid, not just at the screen level
- [DEC-design_discussion-007] Wrapped shows an explicit 'not yet unlocked, check in a few more days' state before the first month boundary or mini-recap threshold is reached, rather than appearing empty or broken.
  rationale: Wrapped is one of four named nav destinations; a dormant-looking tab reads as a bug rather than a feature that hasn't unlocked yet.
  rejected: Leaving the Wrapped tab in a generic empty state indistinguishable from a broken screen
  constraints: Applies until either the first calendar month boundary or the 5-7+ card mini-recap threshold is met
- [DEC-design_discussion-008] Caption text over generative art requires a defined legibility treatment (scrim, frosted text plate, or adaptive text color sampled from the underlying art), and the bloom reveal requires an explicit Reduce Motion fallback (a gentler crossfade preserving the same haptic beats), decided now rather than left to build-time discovery.
  rationale: Caption legibility against an arbitrary busy composition and Reduce Motion support for the app's single signature moment are both concrete failure risks that a generic 'add accessibility later' approach would miss.
  rejected: Leaving caption contrast unaddressed until a real collision is found in testing; Simply disabling the bloom animation for Reduce Motion with no alternate reveal
  constraints: Reduce Motion fallback must preserve the same haptic beats as the full bloom, only removing the physical motion
- [DEC-design_handoff-001] A single @MainActor @Observable AuraStore, injected via environment, is the sole owner of the canonical last-completed-calendar-day value, entitlement snapshot, and demo-mode state; no view or screen independently queries SwiftData to compute its own notion of 'today' or entitlement.
  rationale: The daily-lock/regeneration-credit shared-day-state rule ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) and entitlement-snapshotting rule ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) are only actually shared if there is one source of truth in code; scattered per-view @Query-based date/entitlement checks are exactly how those two rules would silently drift apart under a clock change.
  rejected: Per-screen @Query-based computation of day-state and entitlement
  constraints: Build phase must implement one AuraStore instance injected via environment, not per-screen state duplication
- [DEC-design_handoff-002] Navigation is a TabView with a fully custom tab bar (not just custom NavigationStack chrome) — stock translucent tab bar material is explicitly rejected because it double-blurs against Dusk Gallery's own frosted surfaces; each tab owns its own NavigationStack driven by a typed route enum (TodayRoute, ArchiveRoute, WrappedRoute), with a single PendingDeepLink value on the store consumed once via .onChange to resolve widget taps into the correct tab + path + Today sub-state.
  rationale: The widget-tap-must-land-on-exact-current-state requirement (DEC-initial_discussion-003, DEC-design_discussion-005) has no concrete implementation path without a programmatic deep-link mechanism external to the view hierarchy; raw NavigationLink(destination:) cannot be pushed into from outside the tree.
  rejected: Stock translucent tab bar material; Raw NavigationLink(destination:) navigation without a typed route/deep-link mechanism
  constraints: Build phase must implement PendingDeepLink + typed route enums, not ad hoc navigation state
- [DEC-design_handoff-003] The widget extension requires an App Group shared container holding cached rendered PNGs plus card/palette metadata; the widget reads only this shared cache and never touches the main app's ModelContext directly.
  rationale: This is invisible until the widget target is actually wired up and easy to skip under time pressure since the main app functions fine without it; without it, the widget cannot read the cached-render architecture already mandated by [REDACTED:high_entropy].
  rejected: Widget reading the app's default sandboxed Documents directory or ModelContext directly
  constraints: Must be an explicit line item (app group identifier, shared container URL) in the build handoff
- [DEC-design_handoff-004] The bloom reveal's 'real engine, not a decorative animation' requirement is concretely defined as: 4 genuine cached intermediate composites (seed-point/palette wash, shape-field placement, particle/line density pass, final color grade) generated once at render time from the actual filter/shader chain, cross-dissolved along the spring timeline with the three haptic beats aligned to the 1→2, 2→3, and 3→4(settle) transitions.
  rationale: Literally re-stepping the CIFilter/Metal composite graph every display frame in sync with a spring curve would jank on older supported devices; without a concrete definition, 'real engine' either becomes a performance trap or gets quietly faked as a crossfade over one pre-rendered static image, which would be invisible in review.
  rejected: Re-running the full filter/shader chain live on every display frame; A crossfade/decorative animation layered over a single pre-rendered final image
  constraints: Build phase must generate and cache all 4 intermediate composites at generation/regeneration time, verifiable as 4 distinct real artifacts, not 1
- [DEC-design_handoff-005] Archive grid uses LazyVGrid with cell identity keyed to each card's canonical date-string ID (never array index), rendering a separately-generated, separately-cached small thumbnail (~400x700) distinct from the full 1080x1920 export artifact.
  rationale: Regeneration replaces a card in place (DEC-initial_discussion-006), so index-keyed identity would show stale content or animate the wrong cell on a regen; loading 30+ full-res exports into a scrolling grid is a real memory risk on older devices, and generating thumbnails at scroll-time would violate the cached-render-only architecture ([REDACTED:high_entropy]).
  rejected: Index-keyed ForEach identity; Rendering full-resolution 1080x1920 images directly in grid cells; Generating thumbnails on-demand at scroll time
  constraints: Thumbnail generation must happen once alongside the full-res export, at card generation/regeneration time
- [DEC-design_handoff-006] Concrete visual-system values are locked: 8pt spacing base with 4/8/12/16/24/32/48 steps; type scale mapped to Dynamic Type styles (Display 34/40 Bold→.largeTitle for Wrapped poster headline only, Title 22/28 Semibold→.title2 for the custom top bar, Card Caption 20/26 Semibold→.title3, Body 17/22 Regular→.body, Subhead 15/20 Medium→.subheadline, Caption 13/16 Medium→.caption); corner radii small 8 / medium 16 / large 24 / pill 999.
  rationale: The phase playbook requires explicit point values with zero adjectives standing in for numbers so a SwiftUI builder can write Theme.swift directly.
  rejected: Leaving spacing/type/radius values as adjectives for the build phase to invent
  constraints: Color hex values for semantic roles still outstanding — see open_risks
- [DEC-design_handoff-007] The caption legibility treatment (DEC-design_discussion-008) is concretely specified as a frosted text plate (12pt corner radius), not a raw drop-shadow, with an automatic fallback rule: if the adaptive/sampled-from-art text color ever computes below 4.5:1 contrast against its background, the UI falls back to the frosted plate automatically rather than relying on every generated composition happening to be legible by construction.
  rationale: A drop-shadow reads cheap against painterly art and fails on light/busy compositions; since composition varies a lot by design, some seed/mood combinations will produce low-contrast adaptive text by construction, so a hoped-for outcome isn't sufficient — a concrete, testable fallback rule is needed.
  rejected: Raw drop-shadow as the sole legibility treatment; Relying on adaptive sampled color without a guaranteed-contrast fallback
  constraints: Fallback trigger (4.5:1 contrast ratio) must be implemented as a real runtime check, not a design assumption
- [DEC-design_handoff-008] No external Claude Design handoff is used for this app; the design spec is delivered as code-ready values (spacing, type, radii, component/architecture specs) for a SwiftUI builder to implement directly.
  rationale: The app's entire visual differentiator is the generative engine's rendered output, which no static mockup tool can produce or meaningfully preview; an external design pass risks anchoring effort on decorative chrome polish while the actual gating problem (does the real CIFilter/Metal composition read as beautiful across 8-10+ seed combinations) can only be solved and judged in code against real rendered output.
  rejected: Producing a Claude Design prompt/upload plan for external mockup of chrome or card templates
  constraints: Build/verify phases must judge visual quality against real rendered engine output, not any external mockup
- [DEC-design_handoff-009] Semantic color roles are locked with explicit light+dark hex values: Background #0B0B12/#F6F5F8, Surface #17161F/#FFFFFF, SurfaceElevated #1F1E29/#FDFCFF, TextPrimary #F2F1F6/#16151C, TextSecondary #A6A3B3/#5B5868, Accent #B98CFF/#7C4DFF, Success #5FD9A4/#1E9E6E, Warning #FFC773/#B8720A, Error #FF7A7A/#D93A3A, Hairline #2A2836@60%/#E4E2EA, plus a distinct DemoBadge tint (amber #FFD37A on #3A2E12 dark, #8A5A00 on #FFF3DC light).
  rationale: Phase acceptance checks require every color role to have both a light and dark hex value; the demo badge specifically needs its own tint (not Accent) so it reads as a status label rather than an interactive control, which also satisfies the existing non-color-differentiation accessibility rule.
  rejected: Reusing Accent violet for the demo badge tint
  constraints: TextPrimary/TextSecondary pairs must maintain 4.5:1 contrast against their respective Background/Surface pairs in both appearances
- [DEC-design_handoff-010] Per-screen empty/error/locked states are specified with concrete copy, icon, and recovery action rather than referenced by name from design_discussion: Today not-yet-checked-in (breathing silhouette + headline/subhead/CTA), store-load-failure (rose triangle icon, 'not lost data' framing, Try Again + Copy Diagnostic Info), Archive empty (gallery-frame icon + CTA to Today), Wrapped locked (dynamic countdown copy picking whichever unlock condition is sooner, plus a secondary link to Today).
  rationale: Cross-referencing an earlier phase's state model by name isn't sufficient for a builder to implement directly; the store-load-failure state in particular needs a support-facing recovery action (Copy Diagnostic Info), since a user told 'your data is inaccessible' with no way to report it is a real support gap.
  rejected: Leaving per-screen state copy as an implicit cross-reference to design_discussion
  constraints: Store-load-failure copy/icon must be visually distinct from any empty state, per DEC-design_discussion-005
- [DEC-design_handoff-011] EmptyStateView and ErrorStateView are single shared, parameterized components (icon, headline, subhead, primary action, optional secondary action) reused across Today, Archive, and Wrapped, rather than bespoke per-screen views; Archive's store-load-failure state reuses the exact same ErrorStateView instance/styling as Today's, not a lookalike.
  rationale: Three hand-built near-identical empty/error views are exactly the kind of duplication that drifts out of sync the first time copy changes in one place and not the others; a single underlying store-load failure visible from two tabs should not produce two different-looking error screens, which would itself look like a bug.
  rejected: Bespoke empty/error view per screen
  constraints: Build phase must implement one EmptyStateView and one ErrorStateView component, parameterized per call site, not per-screen duplicates
- [DEC-design_handoff-012] Full component inventory locked and mapped to screens (Theme.swift, AuraTabBar, AuraTopBar, AuraSilhouetteView, SkeletonPulseView, MoodChipCluster, WordChipCluster, BloomRevealView, AuraCardView, CaptionPlate, StreakChip, RegenerateButton, ShareButton, ArchiveGrid/ArchiveCell, DemoBadge/DemoModeBanner, EmptyStateView/ErrorStateView, WrappedLockedStateView, AuraPlusCard, RestorePurchasesRow, NotificationSettingsRow, DemoModeToggleRow, ConfirmationSheet, ToastBanner); a Wrapped poster is implemented as AuraCardView at a different aspect/composite treatment, not a separate rendering path.
  rationale: Satisfies the phase's component-inventory acceptance check with no screen left implicit; treating the Wrapped poster as a variant of AuraCardView rather than a new rendering path avoids a second place where the cached-render architecture or beauty bar could be implemented inconsistently.
  rejected: A wholly separate rendering/component path for Wrapped posters distinct from the per-card AuraCardView
  constraints: Build phase must implement exactly this component list; new bespoke views should be justified against this inventory, not added ad hoc
- [DEC-design_handoff-013] The round-1 decision to decline external Claude Design handoff (DEC-design_handoff-008) is reaffirmed now that the token/component spec is complete.
  rationale: A complete code-ready spec makes an external static mockup even less valuable, since it would add process without adding information a SwiftUI builder doesn't already have.
  rejected: Revisiting external design now that more detail exists
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Rendering engine is a single CIFilter-based pipeline (stock filters plus custom CIColorKernel/CIWarpKernel where flow-field/particle math needs more control), rendered through one shared CIContext, reused identically for all 4 bloom intermediates, the full-res 1080x1920 export, the archive/widget thumbnail, and the Wrapped poster — no separate Metal/MTKView live-rendering path.
  rationale: A split Metal-for-reveal / CIFilter-for-export architecture would be two rendering implementations that must stay visually consistent, the same two-sources-of-truth bug shape already flagged elsewhere in this project (day-state, widget reload, entitlement snapshots) — except here it would hit the one thing the whole app is graded on.
  rejected: Custom Metal/MTKView shader for the live bloom reveal with a separate CIFilter path for static export
  constraints: All rendered artifacts (bloom intermediates, export, thumbnail, Wrapped poster) must go through the same CIContext/filter graph
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The determinism contract is split into two layers: a pure, synchronous, Codable/Hashable 'recipe' struct (palette index, shape-field topology params, density values, caption index) computed from (date, mood, chips, entitlement snapshot, regeneration nonce) is the actual same-inputs-same-output guarantee and is unit-testable with zero GPU involvement; pixel-level output is only a deterministic function of that recipe on a given device/OS, never claimed or tested as byte-identical across GPU families or OS revisions.
  rationale: Core Image's GPU-backed rendering is not contractually byte-stable across GPU families/OS versions, so testing determinism by comparing exported PNG bytes across Simulator vs. device or across an OS update would produce false failures and misrepresent what's actually guaranteed.
  rejected: Testing/claiming determinism via byte-identical PNG comparison across environments
  constraints: Recipe-struct equality is the CI-testable determinism contract; pixel comparison is only valid within a single process/environment
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] SwiftData schema is defined via VersionedSchema/SchemaMigrationPlan starting at v1, even though only one schema version exists at ship.
  rationale: This app has no server and no sync; the local store is the only copy of the user's history forever, so migration support must exist before it's needed rather than being retrofitted after a v2 schema change already requires it.
  rejected: Plain unversioned SwiftData model, adding migration support only when a schema change is actually needed
  constraints: DayEntry/AuraCard and MonthlyWrapped models must be defined inside a VersionedSchema from the start
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The canonical 'last completed calendar day' value exposed by AuraStore must be derived live from a SwiftData query (max date of non-demo DayEntry records), never cached as a separate scalar in UserDefaults or elsewhere.
  rationale: A cached scalar that can drift from the actual persisted records is the same single-source-of-truth failure mode this project has already caught itself on in other areas (day-state, widget reload, entitlement snapshot), just relocated.
  rejected: Caching the last-completed-day value separately in UserDefaults for quick access
  constraints: Any read of 'today's lock state' must go through a query against persisted DayEntry records
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Standard iOS device/iTunes local backup of the SwiftData store is explicitly permitted and expected, and is distinct from the already-banned CloudKit-mirrored container.
  rationale: These are different mechanisms; conflating ordinary device backup with the prohibited CloudKit sync would incorrectly imply the app needs to actively defeat standard iOS backup behavior.
  rejected: Treating standard device backup as equivalent to the banned CloudKit sync and disabling/excluding the store from backup
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] No location, camera, microphone, health, or contacts access anywhere in the app; export uses ShareLink(item:) with a Transferable image rather than a hand-rolled UIActivityViewController; there is no direct Photos-library write affordance, so no NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription or any other privacy-related Info.plist usage-description key is required.
  rationale: Keeping export strictly share-sheet-based removes an entire permission-denial state (Photos write access) that would otherwise need its own design and test coverage, and matches the app's overall minimal-permissions posture.
  rejected: Adding a direct 'Save to Photos' button requiring NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription; Hand-rolling UIActivityViewController instead of using SwiftUI's native ShareLink
  constraints: If a direct Photos-save feature is ever added later, it must add its own permission state and Info.plist key at that time
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] StoreKitTest/SKTestSession is added as the automated-regression test backbone for purchase, restore, and regeneration-entitlement logic, run in a normal XCTest target, alongside (not instead of) manual .storekit-configuration testing in Simulator for the human-eyeballed paywall/purchase-sheet UX pass.
  rationale: Manual Simulator testing with a .storekit file proves the UI flow works but isn't repeatable by CI or a fast test suite; StoreKitTest can script real Transaction flows including refunds in a normal test target, giving repeatable coverage on the riskiest must-have without overclaiming what Simulator alone can prove for real transaction completion.
  rejected: Relying solely on manual .storekit Simulator testing with no automated StoreKit test coverage
  constraints: StoreKitTest coverage and manual Simulator UX testing are complementary and both required, not either/or
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] BGTaskScheduler and any background-execution primitive are explicitly ruled out; monthly Wrapped generation and widget staleness are computed lazily on next foreground (scenePhase == .active check for 'has the calendar month rolled over') and via the widget's own timeline provider reading the shared App Group cache.
  rationale: There's no server push and no reason to wake the app in the background; foreground-lazy computation has no background-execution budget to fight and can't silently fail to run the way a BGAppRefreshTask can.
  rejected: Using BGAppRefreshTask/BGTaskScheduler to precompute Wrapped or refresh the widget in the background
  constraints: Wrapped/month-rollover checks must be tied to scenePhase transitions or the widget timeline provider, not a background task
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The 8-10+ combination visual-review checkpoint (DEC-prompt_contract-003) is implemented as a concrete architectural deliverable: a debug-only render harness (Xcode Previews or a debug menu screen, stripped from Release builds) that batch-renders a fixed, checked-in set of canonical seed/mood/chip combinations and displays/writes them for side-by-side review; the same harness is reused to validate demo-vs-real visual parity ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) by rendering both demo-seeded and fresh-input cards through the identical pipeline.
  rationale: A one-time manual 'someone eyeballs the Simulator' pass is not a reliable enough mechanism to survive a real build under time pressure; making it a rerunnable, checked-in artifact turns the beauty gate and the demo-parity check into something any reviewer can regenerate and inspect in thirty seconds.
  rejected: Treating the visual-review checkpoint as a one-time manual pass with no persistent harness or artifact
  constraints: Harness must be excluded from Release builds; Harness must render both demo-seeded and fresh-input cards for the parity check, not just the base 8-10+ combination set
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] No CoreML, ARKit, or on-device ML of any kind is used anywhere in the app; restated here as an explicit won't-build guardrail rather than an unstated absence.
  rationale: The app's caption and mood-mapping promise is 'deterministic, curated, never hallucinated' — any future temptation to swap in an ML classifier for 'smarter' mood inference would directly break that promise.
  rejected: Leaving ML/AR exclusion implicit rather than stating it as a guardrail
  constraints: Any future ML/AR proposal must be treated as a scope change requiring its own justification, not a quiet addition
- [DEC-tech_specs-001] Mood vocabulary is fixed at 8 values (Radiant, Calm, Wistful, Restless, Tender, Fierce, Hazy, Hopeful) arranged as a radial wheel for coherent hue-rotation palette mapping.
  rationale: Unblocks the 8-10+ combination visual-review checkpoint (already dependent on this per [REDACTED:high_entropy]) and gives palette derivation a structured basis instead of an arbitrary list.
  rejected: Leaving mood count/ordering unspecified until build time
  constraints: Palette-mapping logic in the renderer must use the wheel ordering, not treat moods as an unordered enum
- [DEC-tech_specs-002] Chip vocabulary is fixed at 24 values across 4 families of 6 (texture, weather, pace, company); user selects 1-2 per check-in.
  rationale: Produces 2,400 mood/chip combinations before the date seed is even applied, giving the seed-space enough richness to make 'meaningfully different days' true by construction.
  rejected: A smaller flat chip list with no family structure
  constraints: Family grouping affects curation/UI grouping only, never selection or seeding logic
- [DEC-tech_specs-003] The generative algorithm hashes (dateKey, moodID, sorted chipIDs, timeOfDayBucket, entitlementSnapshot, regenerationNonce) via SHA256 into a splitmix64 stream, and drives composition through a small deterministic pure-Swift noise implementation (continuous flow-field), not a fixed set of recolored templates.
  rationale: A template-plus-recolor approach is exactly the failure mode the prompt calls out ('same template recolored'); a continuous noise-driven field makes structural variation, not just hue variation, the default outcome.
  rejected: Picking from a small library of fixed shape-field templates and recoloring per seed
  constraints: Debug render harness must include adjacent-seed pairs (same mood, consecutive dates) to catch noise-field degeneracy (banding, near-identical adjacent fields) before ship
- [DEC-tech_specs-004] Captions are composed from 3 independently-tracked fragment pools (opener / mood-core / chip-inflected closer), each with its own 30-day no-repeat window, rather than one flat curated phrase bank per mood.
  rationale: A flat bank can't realistically survive a user who picks the same mood and regenerates daily (up to 60 draws against one mood's pool in 30 days) without heavy curation; combinatorial fragment composition makes exhaustion structurally near-impossible from a modest curated set.
  rejected: One flat per-mood phrase bank sized to avoid 30-day repeats
  constraints: Each fragment slot's no-repeat window is tracked independently via CaptionEligibilityQuery
- [DEC-tech_specs-005] Models, Engine (seed hash/noise/palette/caption selection), and Persistence are pulled into a local Swift Package (AuraKit, file:// reference) linked identically by the app target, the widget extension, and the test target.
  rationale: The widget needs CachedCardMetadata decoding and the test target needs the GPU-free recipe engine (per the recipe/pixel determinism split); a local package guarantees one compiled source instead of the same .swift file added to multiple targets and silently drifting, the same two-sources-of-truth shape this project has flagged repeatedly elsewhere.
  rejected: Adding shared .swift files directly to multiple target memberships
  constraints: AuraKit must have zero UIKit/SwiftUI/CoreImage imports; rendering stays in the app target
- [DEC-tech_specs-006] Date/timezone access is abstracted behind an AuraClock protocol (now(), currentTimeZone()), with SystemClock live and TestClock for XCTest, injected into AuraStore and DayStateResolver.
  rationale: Lets the already-locked DST/backward-clock/date-line rules get fast, deterministic, CI-runnable unit tests instead of relying solely on a human manually flipping the Simulator's clock.
  rejected: Reading Date()/TimeZone.current directly inside AuraStore/DayStateResolver
  constraints: Manual Simulator date/timezone changes remain the acceptance-level check per the decision log; TestClock is additive, not a replacement
- [DEC-tech_specs-007] The main SwiftData ModelContainer lives in the app's default private container; only rendered PNGs (full-res, thumbnail, bloom intermediates) and CachedCardMetadata are written into the App Group shared container for the widget.
  rationale: Keeps the single source of truth (SwiftData store) in the app's own sandbox while giving the widget exactly what it needs (per DEC-design_handoff-003) without exposing ModelContext across the process boundary.
  rejected: Placing the entire SwiftData store inside the App Group container
  constraints: Widget extension never links against or opens the app's ModelContainer directly
- [DEC-tech_specs-008] The debug render harness (already mandated by [REDACTED:high_entropy]) must include adjacent-seed pairs (same mood, consecutive dates) in its canonical combination set, not just diverse combinations.
  rationale: A buggy noise implementation could produce collapsed/near-identical output for adjacent seeds without producing an obviously broken single render; only an adjacent-pair comparison would catch that specific failure mode.
  rejected: Only including maximally diverse combinations in the harness's canonical set
  constraints: Must be checked in as part of the harness's fixed combination list, not left to ad hoc manual selection
- [DEC-tech_specs-009] Regeneration divergence is enforced algebraically via RegenerationDivergenceEngine.perturb — nonzero modular offset on palette index, nonzero XOR mask on the flow-field seed — rather than left to hash-stream probability.
  rationale: A shared hash-stream draw only makes divergence likely, not guaranteed; at real usage scale a coincidental collision on 2+ fields would silently ship a regenerate button that does nothing for some users, directly violating [REDACTED:high_entropy].
  rejected: Drawing regenerated fields from the same hash stream with a different nonce and relying on statistical likelihood of divergence
  constraints: Must be provable via one deterministic unit test (e.g. 500 seed triples, assert >=2-of-3 field divergence, zero flake) rather than a statistical/repeated-run test
- [DEC-tech_specs-010] CompositionFamily (paintBloom, particleField, flowLines) is a first-class recipe field mapping directly to the three visual languages named in the original prompt; the base recipe draws it from its own hash lane, and regeneration forces a different family via the same nonzero-offset mechanism as palette/topology.
  rationale: Without this, the engine would only ever produce one continuous noise-driven visual language regardless of what the prompt promised, and a paid regeneration would only ever be a numeric shift rather than a genuinely different kind of picture.
  rejected: Treating all three named visual languages as flavor text and building only one continuous parameterized noise field
  constraints: If build bandwidth is insufficient to render all 3 families at full quality, cut to 2 families (paintBloom plus one of particleField/flowLines) rather than ship a third at lower quality — beauty bar takes priority over family count
- [DEC-tech_specs-011] Palette library is fixed at 32 total curated palettes; free tier resolves paletteIndex mod 16 (first 16), Aura+ resolves mod 32 (full library), via PaletteLibrary.paletteCount(for:)/resolvePalette(index:tier:).
  rationale: Makes the 'expanded palette library' Aura+ unlock a pure function of the already-snapshotted entitlement rather than a separate runtime toggle, keeping it consistent with the no-retroactive-mutation rule ([REDACTED:high_entropy]).
  rejected: A separate settings-driven palette-unlock flag independent of the entitlement snapshot
  constraints: Palette resolution must read from the EntitlementSnapshot stored on the DayEntry at generation time, never current live entitlement
- [DEC-tech_specs-012] Demo history's anchor date range is computed exactly once, on first demo-mode enable (34-day range ending 1 day before the earliest real DayEntry, or today if none exists), and persisted via DemoAnchorStore; every later render reads the persisted range rather than recomputing.
  rationale: A range recomputed from 'now' on every enable would drift and could eventually collide with real usage dates after enough toggling over a long enough time; computing and freezing it once makes collision structurally impossible permanently, not just today.
  rejected: Recomputing the anchor range relative to 'now' each time demo mode is toggled on
  constraints: 34-day range comfortably exceeds the 30+ day demo history requirement ([REDACTED:high_entropy])
- [DEC-tech_specs-013] MoodTrendAggregator.chartData(entries:range:granularity:) returns [MoodTrendDataPoint] (bucketDate, mood, count) directly consumable by Swift Charts BarMark; demo-flagged entries participate in the aggregate identically to real entries, with no separate exclusion logic since the demo/real distinction is already handled visually at the archive-badge/banner level.
  rationale: Turns a vague 'aggregation function' into a concrete, chart-ready contract, and avoids inventing a second demo-labeling mechanism when the archive's per-cell badge already satisfies the non-empty-and-honest requirement for trend data.
  rejected: A generic dictionary/tuple aggregation function requiring the UI layer to reshape it for Charts; Excluding demo entries from the trend aggregate by default

## 0. Fast rules (read first)

- Prefer `@Observable` (Observation framework, iOS 17+) over `ObservableObject`/`@Published` for new view models.
- All UI mutation happens on the main actor. Never call SwiftUI/UIKit off-main.
- `Task {}` inherits the enclosing actor and priority; `Task.detached {}` inherits neither. Know which you want.
- A view's `body` is a pure function of its inputs. It can run many times per second — keep it cheap and side-effect-free.
- Every `ForEach` element needs a **stable** identity. Never key on array index for mutable data.
- `@State` is for view-local, view-owned, transient state — nothing else.
- When generating a project headlessly, the `.pbxproj`/target membership, bundle id, and signing config matter as much as the Swift code. A perfect source file that isn't in the target does not compile.

## 1. Main-thread / UI updates

### 1.1 Mutating UI state from a background thread

**Symptom:** Purple runtime warning "Publishing changes from background threads is not allowed"; UI updates late, flickers, or crashes; `_dispatch_assert_queue_fail`.

**Cause:** State that drives the UI is written from a background queue (e.g. a `URLSession` completion handler, a `DispatchQueue.global` block, a C callback).

**Fix — hop to the main actor before touching UI state:**

```swift
// WRONG: completion handler runs on a background thread
URLSession.shared.dataTask(with: url) { data, _, _ in
    self.items = decode(data)   // ❌ background-thread UI mutation
}.resume()

// RIGHT: async/await keeps you on the caller's actor
@MainActor
func load() async throws {
    let (data, _) = try await URLSession.shared.data(from: url)
    items = try JSONDecoder().decode([Item].self, from: data) // ✅ on main
}
```

If you're stuck with a callback API, bridge explicitly:

```swift
someLegacyAPI { result in
    Task { @MainActor in
        self.items = result   // ✅ explicit hop to main
    }
}
```

- Do **not** sprinkle `DispatchQueue.main.async` everywhere as a superstition. Model the actor boundary once (usually `@MainActor` on the view model) and let the compiler enforce it.
- `@Observable` classes are **not** implicitly main-actor. Mark the type `@MainActor` if it owns UI state.

### 1.2 Blocking the main thread with sync work

**Symptom:** Frozen UI, dropped frames, watchdog `0x8badf00d` termination on launch, a spinner that never spins.

**Cause:** File I/O, JSON decoding of large payloads, image resizing, or `Data(contentsOf:)` on the main thread.

**Fix — move CPU/IO work off-main, then return the result. Prefer the async `byPreparingThumbnail` API, which does the decode/resize off the main thread and never blocks:**

```swift
@MainActor
func thumbnail(from data: Data) async -> UIImage? {
    guard let image = UIImage(data: data) else { return nil }
    // Decode + downsample happen off-main; returns on the calling actor.
    return await image.byPreparingThumbnail(of: CGSize(width: 200, height: 200))
}
```

- Never use `Thread.sleep`, semaphores, or `DispatchGroup.wait()` on the main thread.
- Never do synchronous networking (`Data(contentsOf: remoteURL)`) — it blocks and is not cancellable.

## 2. async/await, Task, and @MainActor

### 2.1 `Task {}` vs `Task.detached {}`

**Symptom:** Either an unexpected main-thread hop, or a data-race warning, depending on which you picked by accident.

**Rule:**
- `Task {}` **inherits** the current actor, priority, and task-local values. Inside a `@MainActor` type, its body runs on the main actor.
- `Task.detached {}` inherits **nothing** — no actor, no priority, no task-locals. Use it only for genuinely independent background work (and reach for it rarely; a `nonisolated` async function is usually the cleaner way to get off-main).

```swift
@MainActor
final class FeedModel {
    var state: LoadState = .idle
    let api: API

    init(api: API) { self.api = api }

    func refresh() {
        Task {                    // ✅ runs on MainActor; safe to touch state
            state = .loading
            let feed = (try? await api.fetch()) ?? []
            state = .loaded(feed)
        }
    }
}
```

- Prefer structured concurrency (`async let`, `TaskGroup`) over spawning unstructured `Task {}` when results must be awaited.

### 2.2 Fire-and-forget tasks that outlive the view

**Symptom:** "Modifying state during view update" logs; work continues after the view disappears; wasted network calls; crashes touching a deallocated model.

**Fix — bind the task lifetime to the view with `.task`:**

```swift
struct FeedView: View {
    @State private var model = FeedModel(api: .live)

    var body: some View {
        List(model.items) { ItemRow(item: $0) }
            .task { await model.load() }   // ✅ auto-cancelled on disappear
    }
}
```

- `.task(id:)` re-runs when `id` changes and cancels the previous run — the correct way to react to a changing parameter (e.g. a selected user id).
- A bare `Task {}` in `onAppear` is **not** cancelled automatically. Only use it when you truly want a lifetime detached from the view, and store/cancel it yourself.

### 2.3 Ignoring cancellation

**Symptom:** A search-as-you-type view fires a request per keystroke and races; stale results overwrite fresh ones.

**Fix — debounce inside `.task(id:)`, which cancels the previous run on each new keystroke:**

```swift
.task(id: query) {
    do {
        try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(300)) // debounce; throws on cancel
        results = try await search(query)
    } catch {
        // CancellationError from a superseded keystroke, or a search failure.
        // Either way, don't overwrite fresh results with stale/empty data.
    }
}
```
